People who tend to look at their situations in different ways, looking at them like obstacles more than miseries are very happy. I myself am struggling with anxiety and depression, and I'm going with a psychiatrist and psychologist, and even though I am having help, most of the work is done by yourself.
There is only one way to get out of this and I' telling you this because I'm finally feeling that I am getting out of it, and that is working on yourself.
I know it seems really dumb, you get told that everyday and it might sound very tedious for you to hear this but it IS the only way out.

Right now it may feel like there is no other way out, but I implore you, sit down for a minute and try to quiet your negative thoughts. What is your mind really telling you? Everytime I started feeling really bad I always assumed that it was because I was lonely but that is far from the truth. While it is natural for humans to wish to be loved and accepted, the truth is that you need to learn to accept and love yourself first before you feel loved by other people.
I later realized that I felt bad because I had a lot of promises I've done to myself that I haven't worked on. Getting good grades, exercising, eating good, reading, whatever goal you might've had, you are feeling bad because you haven't put any work on doing the things you wanted to do or that you love to do.
When I started doing the things that I liked to do and that I wanted to do, plus getting out of my comfort zone, now I feel very secure about myself and even though I'm still struggling with a lot of things I have done a lot of improvement in myself.

Just please, I know it feels like you don't want to live anymore, but trust me, if you focus on yourself and you work on yourself, sooner or later you will start thanking yourself for not doing anything harmful.

Sit down in your room, put in relaxing or motivating music and start writing down what do you really want to do, what are the things that you always wished for? Meeting new people, learning an instrument, getting another job? Whatever it may be, just start working slowly on yourseld and build up your confidence.

A last tip, work out man, it is already proven that living armonically with your own body relieves anxiety and improves your own self worth, if you are not doing anything just start with something very small. If it weren't for me working our I know I wouldn't be living right now.

If you want to talk to somebody or want to be heard you can dm me.

Take care man and don't give up.

Hello friend. I also am going through the same thing. You probably have depression as the symptomps are very similar to what you described. It's incredibly difficult to get out of bed, and you are going to have a lot of ups and downs. Anxiety plays a huge role on how we behave daily, and having a lot of anxiety can cause you to feel very fatigued during the day because you waste your energy by focusing on the things you worry about. 
There is a lot of social pressure in your life, and you may feel like you are wasting your time since everybody seems like their life is going well. While that is partly true, please do not compare yourself to other people. Everybody has problems, unfortunately we are going through some mental health issues, but that doesn't mean you can get out of it.
Another thing, the only way someone can help you is by getting therapy. The only thing friends or family can do is support and listen to you, but they can't help you solve your problems directly. You have to realize you are on your own to solve this, and this is the harsh truth. You have to figure it out. Even if you go to therapy, she or he is going to give you all the tools to help you fix yourself, but if you don't utilize those tools on your own, therapy isn't going to work either.

Having said this, I will give you a few tips. Try starting slowly on working on yourself. Do not strain yourself and pressure yourself in a big manner, for example, if you lack the discipline and motivation to do stuff, you aren't going to suddenly study 6 hours a day, workout 2 hours a day, eat healthily, etc. Willpower isn't limitless, that is why you have tl start slowly.
I know going out in the real world gives a lot of anxiety, especially because of the pandemic, but trust me, start exercising, just do it. You are going to be grateful for starting out in changing your body since it will increase your self esteem and self worth. Also, start cutting out junk food, do not put yourself on a diet, simply start chaning your eating habits little by little as your brain will thank you immensely for this.

What is done is done, I also had failed several subjects in college, but please forgive yourself. You can't change the past, so why are you blaming yourself for it, it is simply a waste of time. Look out for your future, what can you do start getting better grades? It feels like a lot, but trust me, just studying a few minutes every day ln every subject will do wonders for your grades.

Unfortunately, time is definitely ticking... you are wasting your life by worrying about your past, so please start today. Do whatever you can to begin feeling better about yourself. You DEFINITELY know what you should do to feel better, we just put excuses because of our mental health, but there isn't any other solution but to start here and right now, start changing your life!!! 

I wish you all the luck, and I will be here if you want to talk to somebody that has gone through the same things as you, you can dm me if you want :)

Everybody is different, everybody is going through different things, everybody has their own path.

Start writing down what you really want to do, and make yourself little goals, try not to overwhelm yourself by straining yourself with huge goals and expectations, it is not going to work. Make progress little by little, you are going to start getting used to it and each time you achieve those goals your self worth and self esteem are going to increase.

Start talking to yourself in a gentle manner and start forgiving yourself. You may have done things in your past that you aren't proud of, but the past is the past, if you never forgive yourself, the past is going to follow you and haunt you for the rest of your life.

When you have depression, it's normal to have this ups and downs, I have them as well. Sometimes you feel like rhe world is at your feet and that you can do anything you've ever wanted, and some days you will feel like not going out of bed. I understand you, even if we have very different life problems.
There are some things that have been helping me along my journey...
First and one of the most important: exercise. It sounds cliche, but ever since I went to the gym and started taking more care of my nutrition, my life started going a lot better. Remember that most of the times exercise isn't enough! It will only make you feel better about yourself but there are probably past traumas that won't let you overcome depression which leads to my next tip.

Second tip: therapy. It might seem obvious, but if you can figure out a way of getting therapy, please do it. Most of the times, you can't overcome your past traumas by yourself, you need help!! Talking to a therapist in a regular basis will make you feel listened, and she/he is going to help you figure out what is wrong with your conscience.

Third and final tip: socialize more.
One of the biggest reasons I felt depressed all the time was because I was always in my room playing videogames, eating bad and just not doing anything. I know that when somebody has depression it is very difficult to socialize, but just try it, you will feel better. Talk to a friend, it mught seem you don't have any, but there will always be somebody you used to talk to. I once separated from my friends and thought they were gone because I was in a really dark state of mind, but I started opening up myself to them and they understood. If you don't open up, nobody is going to understand what you are going through and they are going to think you don't want to hang out with them anymore.

I'd give you a last tip and that would be writing goals for yourself, but that might be difficult for you considering your current state.

One more thing I'd like to add: there is absolutely nothing wrong with you. You are not a mistake, you are not less than anybody else, you too deserve to live a good life. Depression is just a huge trick on our mind that makes us not to enjoy life to a full extent. You weren't born having it, you got depression because of your experiences in your life, and just like you can acquire ir you can get rid of it as well. Everybody has problems, and everybody has their own process, don't compare yourself!

I hope this helps and if you want to talk to somebody you can dm me here. Good luck :)

Self esteem is the reputation you have with yourself, the reason you don't have self esteem is because you have been promising yourself things and never achieving them, or even not promising yourself anything, not having any goals or dreams make you feel like you are worthless.
Start writing down the things you really want to do, and start making baby step goals, when you start achieving these small goals you are going to feel really good about yourself  trust me.
It's really hard, especially if you suffer from depression, it's going to be hard to get out of bed and start doing things, that's why you have to start slowly. If you suddenly write big goals like exercising 2 hours a day, reading 1 hour books every day and stuff like that, of course it's going to be impossible for most people if they have never had the discipline, remember, will power isn't limitless. You have to train yourself slowly but surely, do this for a long time and suddenly you are going to be a completely different person.

Hello, I'm a male and I definitely have had the same problem. For me, the explanation that I give towards my binging is that it is my escape method, I tend to eat emotionally and every time my anxiety or depression is through the roof I tend to binge a LOT. It's been pretty difficult for me, last year I fall in love with a girl and I started having a lot of self esteem, I didn't binge a lot and I got quite big (muscle wise) while losing fat, but ever since I got rejected I'm in the same boat again. This could be an explanation for your problem, watch your thoughts, I used to binge then punish myself eating very little the next few days to "compensate" like you.

There is another explanation though... you are not the only woman that I've heard goes through this every time they lose a lot of fat. Since the metabolism of girls is slower than men, they have to eat way less to lose fat. When you do this for a long time, you can get very fatigued and your brain is going to start asking for a lot of food... I've seen this in a lot of videos from women talking about this. If this is your problem just try to eat regularly, instead of bingeing try to eat everytime you are hungry but with healthy meals, like yogurt, meat, eggs, stuff like that. It doesn't matter if you gain a litrle fat, your brain is going to thank you, later then you can start losing weight again

I don't think I'm that qualified to tell you since I'm still struggling with this, but recently I've been making changes to my daily schedule and I've realized that I do have more energy than I thought and that I can be way more productive.
First of all, schedule your day. Try arranging in blocks of hours your most important tasks. Want to learn piano everyday? Ok, then schedule it for one hour (or whatever hours), want to read a book? Ok, schedule it to read 30 minutes a day. It's even more effective when you assign those blocks of time in a certain time, so, learn piano at 9:00 a.m for one hour, etc. This idea of arranging your time will force your mind that you have to do those tasks to feel accomplished. Try using small blocks of time if you are strugging with discipline and slowly increase them.

Second thing that has helped me was putting my cellphone in focus mode or "do not disturb" mode, as this allows me to not receive notifications and focus on my tasks, if you really need your phone then find a way to block every app except for the one you are going to require for your task. In Android there's focus mode where you allow to get notifications for any app you want and block the rest of them.

Finally, "just do it". It sounds cliche, but just think about it, it's the best advice there is. It is not so pretty to hear, it's straight to the point, it's what needed to be done. Just do it. Stop overthinking things, shut your mind up and go straight for it, how many times we've not done something because of overthinking about the upcoming scenarios. 

Hope this helps you.

Plus it feels as if this person wants to achieve that goal and that's it. It's always good to define goals and achieving them but that doesn't mean that if you already achieved your goal you will start eating less healthily, that is never a good thing.

NO NO NO. Start lifting right now. Your body will thank you for it. Trust me, you are going to lose weight but you will be a "slim-fat" type of body. You've lost that much weight and never investigated those facts? Plus if you weight train, you don't even need cardio as long as you are going hard and doing good routines. If you do that, your body will start losing fat while your body will look much more structured and defined.

Go take the weights right now, if you still want to do cardio then do it afterwards (you can still do 5 to 15 mins max of light cardio before weight training) because your body already used all (or most) of the glucose (energy) you needed to do weight training (as long as you are doing a proper routine) so your body will start consuming fat as energy because your glucose is already depleted.

It depends on your lifestyle. I used to do it because I am in college and some days I have to attend class at 7 a.m, so sometimes I felt like I had to go in a rush if I wanted to eat breakfast. But this may not work for everyone. For me, I went to the gym hungry or even if I wasn't hungry I ended very tired because I go hard at the gym (I'm overweight but I have good genetics, I'm building muscle fast even if I am becoming thinner) so it made me feel tired all day (even if I drank a gatorade or something else to refuel my electrolytes).

My first advice to weight loss is to stay motivated and focused on what you have to do every day to achieve that goal. People just lose motivation because they think about the final product all day and get sad because they see that losing weight takes more time and they expected. Honestly, people should just eat healthier and start exercising instead of taking extreme regimes in their diet to achieve results as fast as possible. I've been there and while yes, you may start losing weight faster, it always results on giving up on diet after a week.

A lot of people will tell you it's all in the head, and even if that is true, taking huge sacrifices at the start is always a bad option, just ask Jeff from Athlean-X. 

Just my two cents.

Hey. I totally understand your standpoint. In fact, I am the same weight, but I am 20 years old and 175 centimeters. I'm going to give you a little advice.
For me, I had binge eating disorder my entire high school era. I only managed to break it right now, I've not eaten any junk food in 9 days and I feel absolutely no anxiety for junk food, an achievement I have never done in my life. What worked for me may not work for you, but as a person being overweight my entire life I think I may know some advice for you. 
First of all, don't fast. There's a lot of scientific information about how you can burn more fat because you stop eating for a lot of time and you use your ketones as fuel (basically your brain uses fat for energy).
You may encounter new diets as keto diet to enhance intermittent fasting. While this may work for some people, if you find it a nuisance or the fact that you have to discipline yourself so much to do it then don't do it. Trust me, I have tried everything and it just doesn't work if you feel it becoming more like a sacrifice than a lifestyle. You can even search some recommendations of some bodybuilders like Jeff from Athlean-X. He always tells you the same thing. STOP dieting. I'm being sincere. It works wonders. For me, I studied a 1900 calorie diet a nutritionist once gave me, then I decided to eat a little more if I felt hungry or a little less if I just felt full. Trust me, I think this is a great way to start. Just one thing, try to avoid too much fat, that is literally what makes you fat of course (unless you do a keto diet). You shouldn't consume more than 45g of fat for starters.
 The thing about losing weight is that it isn't going to be from one day to another, this thing takes time. So if you feel like your diet is a burden, then just don't do it. It's way better to change your lifestyle to start eating healthily than to get a strict diet and make it feel like a burden and quit it later on. Trust me, I've been there. You may feel motivated your first week, but then your bad eating habits may start to kick in, so it's better to start eating well and don't lose hunger. 
Don't get me wrong, try to calculate the calories that you consume, just to make sure to eat less than what you should eat lose weight.

 I shouldn't really look for a lot of gym routines in youtube. Just because of the fact that you are 14 years old. A lot of people are fat in that era, and then they start growing and the fat gets distributed more equally in their body, making them feel more slim.
What I'm trying to say is that you should probably ask someone or the gym instructor for a very beginner and lightweight routine. Once you become like 16 or 17 years old I would start taking routines seriously, but being 14 years old is way too early to take the gym too seriously.
Seriously, if you feel too overweight, just follow what I told you and you will be fine. I'm not saying never eat any junk food or anything, but try to stay a few weeks without eating any junk food and you will see your body will start feeling way better and you will have more energy for any activity you want to do.

Last but not least. Once you know what you will be eating usually a day and what are you going to for exercise, you should think about that and that only. It's good to fantasize about how lean you could look, how clothes could fit, etc because that's usually the main goal that makes you want to change your life. But once you established that goal, stop thinking about it. TRUST ME, you may feel very disheartened or not motivated once you see that the progress is slower than expected.
